 Chatham Co. unofficial turnout at 53%, early voting rose by about 15,000 ballots compared to last midterm 
 By Joe Hennessy Published : Nov. 4, 2026 at 2:08 PM EST | Updated : 9 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google SAVANNAH, Ga. (WTOC) - Chatham County had a 53% voter turnout in the election, according to an unofficial report from Board of Elections Interim Director Billy Wooten. 
 Wooten said the amount was average for what it normally sees in an election.
 The unofficial numbers, as of Wednesday afternoon, showed more than 112,450 voters in the county.
 Wooten said he expected closer to a 60% turnout with top-of-the-ticket races including the governor’s race and a U.S. Senate race on the ballot.
 Turnout numbers
 The report showed on Wednesday that about 45,100 people voted on Election Day, more than 62,750 people voted in advance, and 4,580 voted by mail-in absentee ballot.
 Provisional ballots have not been counted yet.
 Wooten said there were about 15,000 more early ballots submitted this year compared to the last midterm election.
 “[Tuesday], we had not quite 46,000 to vote, which is good, but four years ago for the last midterm we almost hit 50 [thousand] so we were under that total,” Wooten said.
 Poll watchers
 As WTOC reported, the Department of Justice said they would send a record number of election monitors , more than 1,000 of them, across the country.
 Wooten believed at that time that around six to 10 would move around Chatham Co. polling locations.
 On Wednesday, he said there were only five.
 “We had very few instances at the polls where we had to ask either voters, or poll watchers, or observers, to calm down or to stop doing something that they were involved in. We really had a good day at the polls,” Wooten said. “We have more than 80 polls, they just picked a few polls. I know they were in Port Wentworth, I talked with one, but I did not meet with them.”
 Next steps
 Wooten said the board will reconcile and consolidate the reports to give to the state. The board will work with the local board for certification of the ballots.
 The board is waiting to see if candidates will fight the results, which could delay the official results. Wooten said that is part of the process, and people who win want to prove it, and people who lose want proof, too.
 Unofficial results in select races
 These numbers were available after 12 p.m. on Wednesday, November 4. All of the numbers are unofficial and will be reviewed.
 Governor:
 Keisha Lance Bottoms (D) received 70,190 votes 
 Rick Jackson (R) received 41,326 
 Lt. Governor:
 Josh McLaurin (D) received 71,954 votes 
 Greg Dolezal (R) received 39,276 votes 
 U.S. Senate:
 Jon Ossoff (I)(D) received 75,230 votes in Chatham Co. 
 Mike Collins (R) received 36,600 votes 
 Secretary of State:
 Penny Brown Reynolds (D) received 71,506 votes 
 Tim Fleming (R) received 39,866 votes 
 Attorney General:
 Tanya Miller (D) received 71,395 votes 
 Brian Strickland (R) received 40,142 votes 
 Commissioner of Agriculture:
 Katherine E. Juhan-Arnold (D) received 69,235 votes 
 Tyler Harper (I)(R) received 41,867 votes 
 U.S. House of Representatives District 1:
 Amanda Hollowell (D) received 72,216 votes 
 Jim Kingston (R) received 39,236 votes 
 State House of Representatives District 161:
 David Dillie (D) received 7,023 votes 
 Bill Hitchens (R) received 2,625 votes
